findings.finding: The fix moves subagent oversize enforcement from "blocks the orchestrator's Stop (annoyingly, but it did surface the oversize state)" to "delegated to the subagent's F0/F11 finalization." But per the spec's own Architecture Review finding #2, `bloat_gate_on_stop.py` never fires with `agent_id` in production (registered on `Stop` only, never `SubagentStop`). So the new `bloat_pending.<sid>.<agent_id>.json` markers are written by the subagent's PostToolUse but read by no one — AC #3 is a "defensive-correctness property," not a live path. The entire enforcement burden now rests on the claim that F0/F11 finalization checks file sizes against the same 300/400-line ceiling. If F0/F11 is a lighter-weight check (or is skipped when a runner crashes/times out), this fix converts a false-positive block into a silent enforcement gap for all subagent edits.
findings.suggestion: Verify empirically that F0/F11 enforces the identical ceiling on the same file set — quote the enforcement point in the spec rather than citing `campaign-worktree.md` architecturally. If it doesn't, registering the gate on `SubagentStop` as well (so the subagent's own terminal event consumes its own marker) is a small, targeted addition that makes AC #3 a real path instead of dead-correct code.  2. Category: dependency — Severity: low

findings.finding: Any existing cleanup/janitor logic that removes marker files by exact session key (`bloat_pending.<sid>.json` on session end, lock-dir sweeps, dashboard tooling that reads markers) will now miss the agent-suffixed variants. The spec's boundary table covers only the writer→gate pair; it doesn't establish whether anything else in the repo globs or deletes these files.
findings.suggestion: Grep for `bloat_pending` consumers outside the two hook scripts. If a session-end cleanup exists, it needs the same composite-key treatment; if none exists, note that explicitly so a future reader doesn't assume one.  3. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Subagent markers that are written but never consumed (per finding 1, no live reader) accumulate in `.shipwright/locks/` until TTL — and TTL appears to mean "ignore if older than 1h," not "delete." Each spawned subagent with an oversize touch creates a new uniquely-keyed file; agent_ids are per-spawn, so repeated campaign runs produce one orphan file per subagent incident, persisting indefinitely on disk even after expiry.
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether anything ever unlinks expired marker files. If not, a one-line "delete if expired" check in whichever hook touches the locks dir next is cheap; if the volume is genuinely negligible, document that decision the way finding #3 in the Architecture Review did.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: The writer-side resolution path: when a subagent subsequently shrinks a file back under ceiling, its PostToolUse runs with the same `agent_id`, so it updates the correct suffixed marker — this is fine and covered. But if the subagent dies mid-edit (context limit, task kill), its marker persists with no agent left to resolve it. Pre-fix this blocked the orchestrator (the bug); post-fix it's inert until TTL, which is the intended behavior — just worth confirming the orchestrator's gate doesn't fall back to any "read all markers for this session" mode under error conditions (e.g., malformed payload where `agent_id` parsing fails and the gate silently degrades to session-only matching).
findings.suggestion: Verify the marker-key function's failure mode on malformed payloads (missing `session_id`, non-string `agent_id`) is an explicit, tested behavior, not an incidental one — the whitespace-only test suggests the team already thinks this way, so extend it one step to absent/malformed `session_id`.  5. Category: approach — Severity: low (positive)

findings.finding: The core approach is sound and I have no design objection: keying on the composite `(session_id, agent_id)` is the correct root-cause fix, the hex-escape bijection for sanitization is the right call over lossy substitution (architecture review finding #1 was correctly handled), and the no-`agent_id` path preserving byte-identical keys means zero migration burden. The rejected alternative (runner self-resolve) was correctly identified as fixing the symptom, not the defect. The stale-marker TTL decision (architecture finding #3) is a reasonable bounded-rollout trade.

The plan still implies subagent self-enforcement through a “Stop-class event,” but the registered gate runs on `Stop`, not `SubagentStop`. The later architecture note correctly narrows this to a defensive property, yet the acceptance criterion and alternative rationale retain the stronger production claim.
findings.suggestion: Update the acceptance criterion and plan wording to state explicitly that this change provides marker isolation only. Separately verify that F0/F11 finalization does not depend on this Stop marker being consumed; otherwise wire and test an actual `SubagentStop` consumer.

findings.finding: Even if `agent_id` encoding is collision-free, the composite filename can still be ambiguous if `session_id` may contain the separator. For example, a session-only key `a.b` and a composite `(a, b)` both produce `a.b`. UUID-only session IDs may make this unlikely today, but the format is a producer/consumer boundary and should not silently rely on an undocumented restriction.
findings.suggestion: Confirm and document that `session_id` cannot contain `.`. If that guarantee is unavailable, use an unambiguous suffix format while preserving the legacy no-agent filename exactly, such as `bloat_pending.<legacy-session>.agent-<encoded-agent>.json`.

findings.finding: Existing old-format subagent markers remain under the parent session key until TTL expiry and can continue blocking the orchestrator during rollout. This is acknowledged, but deployment behavior is not stated.
findings.suggestion: Document the one-hour transient explicitly in release/operational notes and ensure rollback does not leave operators confused by mixed-format markers.  Overall, the root-cause fix is sound and appropriately small, with strong regression coverage. Resolve the live subagent-enforcement wording and make the key composition unambiguous before merging.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

### Implementation vs. spec

The core fix is correct. `marker_key()` in `bloat_marker_key.py` reproduces the prior session-only key exactly when `agent_id` is absent (payload `session_id` -> stripped env var -> `unknown`, same strip semantics in both branches), so AC #4's byte-identical requirement is satisfied by inspection. Docs updates cover both rows (AC #5). AC #3 is honestly scoped in the docs as a defensive property rather than a live path.
